name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund spread about 152bp, above the 150bp Alert line; OFCE put it at 163bp on 3 Nov
state: France's 10-year yield was 4.77% on 6 Nov, down from 4.95% on 3 Nov, against about 3.25% on the German Bund, a spread near 152bp (Trading Economics). OFCE, the French economic institute, put the gap at 1.63 points on 3 Nov, a level not seen since the euro-area debt crisis. Fitch moved France's outlook to negative on 3 Nov. No failed G7 auction or emergency ECB buying has been reported.
for_you: Wider spreads raise French government borrowing costs; OFCE estimates about €7.4bn a year by end-2027.

sources.title: Trading Economics — France 10-year government bond yield
OFCE — Cost to public finances of the spread between French and German bond yields

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
